title: Silk Roads: Zarafshan–Karakum corridor
summary: An 866 km World Heritage corridor of 34 sites in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. It follows the Zarafshan River west, then old caravan roads across the Karakum Desert to the Merv oasis, linking Samarkand, Bukhara and Merv. UNESCO dates its use from the 2nd century BCE to the 16th century CE, with peaks when Sogdian merchants rose, in trade with the Muslim world, and under Mongol rule.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO gives the 2nd century BCE to the 16th century CE; its own list of prosperous periods runs the Mongol-era one to the 17th century. Samarkand was a way station from the 4th century BCE (Smithsonian).

beats.caption: Caravans follow the Zarafshan River west and cross the Karakum Desert to the Merv oasis.
Sogdian merchants rise, the first of the corridor's three prosperous periods.
For some eighteen centuries goods, ideas and beliefs pass along the corridor, leaving mosques, caravanserais and cities.
